summary: Survey existing PetPattern subsystems vs release-hardening requirements to avoid rebuilding done work

implemented: Schema versioning (req 2): SCHEMA_VERSION=1 constant is stamped on every row server-side (AnalyticsService.java:37,96); schema_version is NOT NULL in the entity/table (AnalyticsEvent.java:44-45, V14__analytics_events.sql:21). Client-supplied schemaVersion in the DTO is ignored, so the server is authoritative.

Platform + appVersion capture (req 3): platform is constrained to {web,android,ios} with a 'web' fallback and appVersion is regex-validated (^[0-9A-Za-z.+_-]{1,20}$) then stored (AnalyticsService.java:39,43,94-95,145-148; AnalyticsEvent.java:38-42). Ingest endpoint accepts both from mobile clients (AnalyticsController.java:58).

Pseudonymous account ref (req 4): ref = Base64url(SHA-256(ownerId + ':' + salt)); the raw owner id is never stored (AnalyticsService.java:104-114; AnalyticsEvent.java:26-27). Verified by tests (AnalyticsServiceTest.java:26-44).

UTC timestamps (req 5): occurredAt=Instant.now() and occurredOn=now.atZone(ZoneOffset.UTC).toLocalDate() (AnalyticsService.java:88-93); column is 'timestamp with time zone' (V14:17); report uses LocalDate.now(ZoneOffset.UTC) (AnalyticsController.java:75).

Authorized report endpoint, not public (req 9): GET /api/analytics/report requires header X-Analytics-Token; 404 when no admin-token is configured (disabled by default), 403 on mismatch via constant-time MessageDigest.isEqual (AnalyticsController.java:63-85; application.yml:118-120 default empty).

D1/D7/D30 retention (part of req 10 & 11): cohort = ref's first UTC day, retained if any event exactly N days later, in-progress cohorts excluded so they don't deflate the rate (AnalyticsReportService.java:60-89). Well-defined windows + timezone handling, covered by deterministic test (AnalyticsReportServiceTest.java:18-49).
Funnel metric (part of req 10): distinct-users + total per event type, sorted desc (AnalyticsReportService.java:32-37; AnalyticsEventRepository.java:16-18).
Fail-safe recording (req context): all recording is wrapped so analytics never throws into a request (AnalyticsService.java:83-101).

Frontend client + privacy tests: frontend/src/analytics.js sends only {event, ts} for an allow-listed event set via sendBeacon/keepalive, no-op unless VITE_ANALYTICS_URL is set; guarded by frontend/src/analytics.test.js. Wired at App.jsx:156-157,678,747,800,856 and AccountView.jsx:32,59.
partial: 23-event model (req 1): only 7 event types exist in AnalyticsEventType.java:17-23 (registered, pet_created, checkin_created, pattern_viewed, vet_summary_viewed, export_clicked, account_deleted). Of the 23 required, ~5 map cleanly: ACCOUNT_REGISTERED->REGISTERED, PET_CREATED, PATTERN_VIEWED, DATA_EXPORT_REQUESTED->EXPORT_CLICKED, ACCOUNT_DELETED. VET_SUMMARY_GENERATED is only loosely covered by VET_SUMMARY_VIEWED (different semantics). The granular check-in taxonomy (SAME_AS_USUAL/CHANGED_DAY) is not distinct events — only a 'mode' meta value on a single CHECKIN_CREATED event, and the allowed modes (quick/full/changed/same_as_yesterday, AnalyticsService.java:40) don't match the required names.

Metadata allow-list (req 6): a strict allow-list exists and strips unknown keys / rejects invalid values / never stores PII or health text (AnalyticsService.java:120-142; tests AnalyticsServiceTest.java:47-67), BUT it is a single GLOBAL allow-list (species, mode) applied to every event type — it is NOT per-event as required. Any event can carry species/mode; there is no per-type key schema.

Idempotent milestones (req 7): the generic once-per-ref mechanism exists (AnalyticsEventType.isOncePerRef + repository.existsByRefAndType, AnalyticsService.java:85-86) but is applied ONLY to REGISTERED and ACCOUNT_DELETED. The specific required milestones (FIRST_CHECKIN, THIRD_USEFUL_CHECKIN, SEVENTH_USEFUL_CHECKIN, FIRST_WEEKLY_OVERVIEW, FIRST_PATTERN_GENERATED) do not exist, so first/3rd/7th-useful-checkin idempotency is not implemented. Also the exists-then-save guard is not atomic: no unique constraint on (ref,type) exists in V14 (only PK on id + two non-unique indexes), so concurrent milestone writes could double-fire.

Deleted account/pet handling (req 8): account deletion is handled deliberately — ACCOUNT_DELETED is recorded before wipe and pseudonymous rows intentionally survive since there is no FK/identity (AccountController.java:53-64). But there is no explicit purge of analytics on deletion, and deleted-PET handling is effectively absent (no pet id is stored, so nothing is done on pet deletion). Adequate as a privacy design but not an explicit deletion-reconciliation feature.

Report metrics (req 10): funnel + D1/D7/D30 are present, but PLATFORM ATTRIBUTION is missing — AnalyticsReportResponse.java has no platform breakdown and AnalyticsEventRepository has no per-platform query; platform is stored but never surfaced in the report.

Definitions (req 11): D1/D7/D30 windows, timezone (UTC), and active-day (any event on a UTC day) are well-defined; but 'useful check-in' is defined nowhere (the THIRD/SEVENTH_USEFUL_CHECKIN concept is absent), and analytics duplicate-prevention only covers the 2 milestone events (non-atomic).
missing: 16 of the 23 required event types are entirely absent: ONBOARDING_COMPLETED, FIRST_CHECKIN_COMPLETED, SAME_AS_USUAL_CHECKIN_COMPLETED (as a distinct event), CHANGED_DAY_CHECKIN_COMPLETED (as a distinct event), THIRD_USEFUL_CHECKIN_REACHED, SEVENTH_USEFUL_CHECKIN_REACHED, FIRST_WEEKLY_OVERVIEW_AVAILABLE, WEEKLY_OVERVIEW_VIEWED, FIRST_PATTERN_GENERATED, PHOTO_TIMELINE_USED, VET_SUMMARY_SHARED, CAREGIVER_INVITED, REMINDER_ENABLED, REMINDER_PERMISSION_GRANTED, REMINDER_PERMISSION_DENIED, REMINDER_NOTIFICATION_OPENED, NOTIFICATION_TO_CHECKIN_CONVERSION.
Milestone events with idempotent 1st/3rd/7th-useful-check-in semantics — no such events exist and there is no 'useful check-in' counter/definition.
Platform attribution in the report (no platform-segmented funnel/retention or platform breakdown query).
Per-event (per-type) metadata allow-list — only one global allow-list exists.
A DB-level uniqueness guarantee for once-per-ref milestones (no unique constraint on (ref,type)); duplicate prevention is a non-atomic read-then-write.

Reminder/notification analytics entirely (all 5 reminder/notification events + notification->checkin conversion) — nothing in the analytics layer records reminder permission state or notification-driven conversions.
Any test for the report endpoint's authorization (no AnalyticsControllerTest exists — 404/403/token paths are untested).
risks: The privacy/retention foundation is genuinely solid and well-tested — do NOT rebuild it. The gap is breadth of the event taxonomy and report dimensions, not the core mechanics.
RetentionSummary.java is unrelated to product analytics (it is the per-pet habit/streak widget in the check-in domain); the task listed it but it is not part of the analytics event pipeline.

The web frontend (analytics.js) posts to an EXTERNAL collector (VITE_ANALYTICS_URL) sending only {event, ts}, while the backend records the same 7-event vocabulary server-side into analytics_event. These are two parallel pipelines; the backend /api/analytics/events ingest endpoint is used only by mobile clients, not the web app.

Once-per-ref milestone dedup is read-then-write with no DB unique constraint on (ref,type); low practical risk today (only registration/deletion) but would break under concurrency if more milestones adopt it.
The report endpoint is entirely untested (no AnalyticsControllerTest), so the 404/403/token authorization contract is unverified by CI.
result.recommendation: 1) Expand AnalyticsEventType to the full 23-event vocabulary (add onboarding, first/3rd/7th-useful-checkin milestones, weekly-overview, pattern-generated, photo-timeline, vet-summary generated/shared, caregiver-invited, and the 5 reminder/notification events + notification->checkin conversion), keeping the wire()/oncePerRef pattern. 2) Define 'useful check-in' explicitly and implement the 1st/3rd/7th milestone counters with an atomic guard — add a UNIQUE(ref, type) constraint (new migration) so once-per-ref cannot double-fire. 3) Add platform attribution to the report: a per-platform funnel/retention query in AnalyticsEventRepository and corresponding fields in AnalyticsReportResponse. 4) Move the metadata allow-list from a single global map to a per-event-type key schema so req 6 is truly per-event. 5) Add an AnalyticsControllerTest covering the 404 (no token), 403 (bad token), and 200 (valid token) paths, plus the ingest endpoint rejecting oncePerRef types. 6) Wire reminder/notification events from the reminder subsystem (WP3) into analytics. The check-in mode meta already models same/changed — promote those to distinct events if the funnel needs them.

implemented: Explicit opt-in: default is OFF (loadReminder returns {enabled:false,...} at reminders.js:13,17) and the reminder only turns on via the user's toggle click (ReminderControl.jsx:35-48). No auto-enable.

Permission requested at the right moment: requested inside the toggle() user-gesture when turning ON, never on page load — native via ensureNativePermission (ReminderControl.jsx:41; nativeNotifications.js:26-37) and web via Notification.requestPermission only when permission==='default' (ReminderControl.jsx:42-43).

Neutral lock-screen copy: reminderBody returns "Time for {name}'s daily check-in." with no health detail (reminderSchedule.js:48-54); native notification uses title 'PetPattern' + that neutral body (nativeNotifications.js:56-57). Only the owner-chosen pet name appears.

Suppress today's reminder after a qualifying check-in — WEB path only: shouldRemind returns false when loggedToday (reminderSchedule.js:24-25), enforced in maybeNotify (reminders.js:38-47) and covered by a test (reminderSchedule.test.js:20).

Disable + cancel on turn-off: toggling off sets enabled:false (ReminderControl.jsx:36-38); the native effect re-runs and syncNativeReminder cancels the scheduled id before returning early (nativeNotifications.js:49-51); the web interval is cleared (ReminderControl.jsx:23-27).

No duplicate scheduled notifications for a single pet on native: a single stable REMINDER_ID=1001 with cancel-before-schedule so re-scheduling replaces rather than stacks (nativeNotifications.js:13,49,53).

Reminder-time-change handling: native re-syncs on every pref change (effect dep [native,pref,pet.name], ReminderControl.jsx:30-33) cancelling+rescheduling with the stable id; web recomputes each minute and de-dups via the per-day .notified key (reminders.js:29-52).

Offline-safe: the reminder system makes no network calls; scheduling is purely local (localStorage + OS). localStorage reads/writes are wrapped in try/catch and maybeNotify bails if storage is blocked (reminders.js:10-26,31-35).

Permission-denied UI state (web): explicit 'Notifications are blocked — enable them in your browser settings' message when permission==='denied' (ReminderControl.jsx:73-74), plus an 'unsupported browser' branch (line 69-70).

App-restart handling: pref persisted to localStorage (saveReminder, reminders.js:20-26); the per-day .notified key prevents a double web nudge across restarts (reminders.js:29-52); native re-syncs on mount so the OS-held repeating notification is re-anchored (ReminderControl.jsx:30-33).
partial: 'Do NOT mark enabled if denied' — BUGGY: toggle() sets pref.enabled=true unconditionally after requesting permission, regardless of the granted/denied result (ReminderControl.jsx:40-47). When denied, the chip still shows the active 'on' state and the pref persists enabled:true; only a note hints it won't work. (Web won't actually fire because maybeNotify guards permission==='granted', but the enabled state is semantically wrong and native still attempts to schedule.)

Permission-denied UI on NATIVE is generic: any non-granted state shows the same 'Allow notifications to get a daily reminder.' note (ReminderControl.jsx:65-68); it does not distinguish denied vs unsupported the way the web branch does.

Account-level vs pet-level is only implicit, not clearly defined: reminders are keyed per pet (storageKey `petpattern.reminder.${pet.id}`, ReminderControl.jsx:8), i.e. pet-level, but the native single-id design (below) collapses this to one slot, contradicting per-pet intent. No documented account-vs-pet model.

Timezone-change / DST handling is only solid on WEB (shouldRemind/localDateKey recompute from device-local time every minute, reminderSchedule.js:12-32). NATIVE has no timezone-change or app-resume re-sync: the notification is anchored once via nextReminderAt and left to Capacitor every:'day' repeat (nativeNotifications.js:51-58); there is no App 'resume' or timezone listener to re-anchor after a DST/timezone shift.

Deep-link opened notification to a safe destination is only partial: mobile.js routes appUrlOpen App/Universal links carrying #reset=/#shared= hashes (mobile.js:18-46), but the scheduled reminder carries no `extra` payload and there is NO localNotificationActionPerformed listener anywhere — tapping the reminder just opens the app's default route. Safe by omission, but not intentionally routed to the pet's check-in.
missing: KEY DEFECT — native reminder still fires after a qualifying check-in: on the native path today's occurrence is never cancelled/suppressed after a check-in. The scheduling effect does not depend on loggedToday (ReminderControl.jsx:30-33) and syncNativeReminder ignores loggedToday entirely, always (re)scheduling a repeating daily notification (nativeNotifications.js:45-61). cancelNativeReminder exists but is never imported/called anywhere (dead export). So a native reminder fires at the chosen time even when the user already logged today — the 'schedule next occurrence keeping recurrence' half works, but the 'cancel/suppress today' half is absent on native.

Multi-pet native collision: REMINDER_ID is a single global constant 1001 shared across all pets (nativeNotifications.js:13). Enabling a reminder for a second pet overwrites the first pet's scheduled notification, so only ONE native reminder can exist at a time. Multi-pet native reminders are effectively broken (mutual clobbering rather than per-pet reminders).

'No swallowed scheduling failures' is violated: syncNativeReminder catches and silently ignores all scheduling errors (nativeNotifications.js:62-64) and maybeNotify swallows Notification-construction errors (reminders.js:53-55). No logging, telemetry, or UI surfaces a scheduling failure. (Partial mitigation on web: the day is marked .notified only after a successful Notification construction, reminders.js:50-52, so a transient failure doesn't permanently suppress that day — but the failure itself is invisible.)

Privacy-safe notification analytics is not wired up: analytics.js exists and is privacy-safe (fixed event-name allow-list, no payload, off unless VITE_ANALYTICS_URL, analytics.js:17-45), but its allow-list contains NO reminder events (no reminder_enabled / reminder_fired / reminder_tapped / permission_denied), and neither reminders.js nor nativeNotifications.js calls track(). There is zero measurement of reminder opt-in, delivery, or engagement.
risks: The headline 'reminder fires after check-in' defect is real and lives ENTIRELY in the native path, which cannot be exercised in this environment (no device/emulator) and has no automated tests — so it will only surface on a real build. nativeNotifications.js itself flags it is 'GENERATED / NOT VERIFIABLE here'.

Test coverage is limited to the pure web-suppression logic: reminderSchedule.test.js covers shouldRemind (incl. loggedToday, permission, per-day de-dup, malformed time), nextReminderAt, and localDateKey. There are NO tests for maybeNotify (web notify + de-dup + swallow), nativeNotifications.js (syncNativeReminder cancel/schedule, multi-pet id collision, ensureNativePermission, unused cancelNativeReminder), ReminderControl.jsx (toggle, enabled-if-denied bug, permission UI states), or mobile.js deep-links. The two most important defects (native fires-after-checkin, multi-pet single-id) are completely untested.
The enabled-if-denied behavior means a user who denies permission still sees an 'on' chip and a persisted enabled:true — a confusing state that reads as working when it isn't.
result.recommendation: "1) Fix the native fires-after-checkin defect: make the native (re)schedule react to loggedToday — pass loggedToday into syncNativeReminder and, after a qualifying check-in, cancel today's occurrence and reschedule starting at the NEXT day's time (keeping every:'day' recurrence). Wire the actual check-in handlers (App.jsx checkin_created, ~lines 800/856) to call cancelNativeReminder/re-sync, and add loggedToday to the effect deps (ReminderControl.jsx:30-33). 2) Fix multi-pet native collision: derive a per-pet notification id (e.g. hash pet.id) instead of the single REMINDER_ID=1001 (nativeNotifications.js:13). 3) Only set pref.enabled=true after a granted permission in toggle() (ReminderControl.jsx:40-47); otherwise leave it off and show the denied state. 4) Surface scheduling failures instead of swallowing them (at minimum log + a track('reminder_schedule_failed')-style event) (nativeNotifications.js:62-64, reminders.js:53-55). 5) Add privacy-safe reminder events to the analytics allow-list (analytics.js:17-25) and fire them on enable/schedule/tap. 6) Add a localNotificationActionPerformed listener that deep-links a tapped reminder to the pet's check-in (safe destination), and attach an `extra` payload when scheduling. 7) Add a native App 'resume'/timezone re-sync so DST/timezone changes re-anchor the scheduled time. 8) Add tests for maybeNotify, syncNativeReminder (cancel/schedule/multi-pet id), and the toggle enabled-if-denied path."

No native camera integration. Pure code-gap.

Tied to the missing native projects + undocumented.

Icon / splash asset generation instructions — docs/mobile.md contains no icon or splash generation guidance; there is no frontend/resources/ folder and no @capacitor/assets or cordova-res tooling; capacitor.config.json references smallIcon "ic_stat_icon" with no instructions to produce it. Pure doc/code-gap.
risks: The native Android/iOS projects do not exist in the repo, so there is nothing to build or ship yet — the 'mobile app' is currently a web build plus generated-but-unverified glue code (docs/mobile.md marks config, native notifications, and deep links 'generated', not verified on device).

Because none of the Capacitor plugin packages are in package.json/lockfile, plugin versions are unpinned and native builds depend on a manual, undocumented-for-Keyboard/Browser/Camera install step — easy to drift from @capacitor/core ^8.4.1.
No offline/network-failure handling means a dropped connection (common on mobile) surfaces raw 'Failed to fetch' errors to users with no graceful state.
Missing Android hardware back-button handling means the OS back gesture will background/exit the app instead of navigating the SPA, a likely Play Store UX rejection risk.

Camera/photo capture via <input type=file> may not reliably access the device camera inside the Capacitor WebView, and without permission usage descriptions an iOS build touching camera/photos can be rejected or crash.

Environment-blocked verification: with no Android SDK (win32) and no Xcode/macOS, the actual native build, deep-link registration (assetlinks/AASA), notification delivery, and permission prompts cannot be verified in this environment — only the JS glue and config can be reviewed.
result.recommendation: Prioritize the pure code-gaps that do not need a device: (1) add an Android hardware back-button listener (App.addListener('backButton')) that drives SPA history/hash navigation and only exits at the root; (2) wrap fetch in frontend/src/api.js to catch network TypeErrors and expose an offline/error state (plus optional navigator.onLine UI); (3) decide on Camera/Keyboard/Browser plugin integration — at minimum add @capacitor/camera for native photo capture or document the <input type=file> fallback as intentional; (4) add icon/splash generation instructions (e.g. @capacitor/assets + a 1024px source and an ic_stat_icon) to docs/mobile.md; (5) pin the plugin packages in package.json instead of relying on a manual install, and add a frontend/.env.mobile + vite mobile-mode wiring so build:mobile injects the prod API base. Then, when a native toolchain is available (environment-blocked here): run `npx cap add android`/`npx cap add ios`, commit the scaffolded projects, author permission usage descriptions (Info.plist / AndroidManifest) for camera/photos/notifications, add assetlinks.json + apple-app-site-association for App/Universal Links, and produce+verify a signed build. The .gitignore signing exclusions (lines 42-59) are already correct and should be kept.

result.wp: WP5 — Secure release packaging & secret hygiene
implemented: No secret is currently tracked in git. `git ls-files` returns only `.env.example` among env/secret-named files; all other matches (ForgotPasswordRequest.java, PasswordResetService.java, V7__password_reset_tokens.sql, ops/backup-db.sh, etc.) are legitimate source for the password-reset feature. No `.env`, keystore, `*.key/*.pem/*.p12/*.jks`, `google-services.json`, `.npmrc`, or `.netrc` is tracked.
Git history is clean of secrets: `git log --all --diff-filter=A` and `git log --all -- '*.env' '.env'` both return nothing — no secret file was ever committed and later removed.

`.env.example` (root) contains safe placeholders only: every secret field (POSTGRES_PASSWORD, SMTP_PASSWORD, GOOGLE_OAUTH_CLIENT_SECRET, ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, GEMINI_API_KEY, PETPATTERN_ANALYTICS_REF_SALT, PETPATTERN_ANALYTICS_ADMIN_TOKEN, SENTRY_DSN, VITE_*) is empty or a non-secret example; header explicitly says '.env is gitignored; never commit real secrets'.

`.gitignore` covers the major sensitive/build paths: `.env` + `*.env` with `!.env.example` re-include, `backups/`, `frontend/node_modules/`, `backend/target/`, `frontend/dist/`, `*.zip`, `*.log`/`*.dump`/`*.sql.gz`/`*.dump.gz`, mobile signing material (`*.jks`,`*.keystore`,`*.p12`,`*.pem`,`*.key`,`key.properties`,`google-services.json`,`GoogleService-Info.plist`), and android/ios build outputs.
`backend/.dockerignore` and `frontend/.dockerignore` both exist and exclude `.env`/`*.env`, `.git`, IDE files, logs, and build output (target / node_modules / dist / coverage).

Application config does not hardcode production secrets: `backend/src/main/resources/application.yml` reads every prod secret from env (`${GOOGLE_OAUTH_CLIENT_SECRET:}`, `${SENTRY_DSN:}`, `${PETPATTERN_ANALYTICS_ADMIN_TOKEN:}`, `${PETPATTERN_AI_API_KEY:...}`), and `docker-compose.prod.yml` sets `SPRING_DATASOURCE_PASSWORD: ${POSTGRES_PASSWORD:?set POSTGRES_PASSWORD in .env}` (fails if unset).

`git archive HEAD` (tracked-only) inherently excludes the untracked local cruft — verified it contains none of `.env`, `backend;C`, `frontend/package.json;C`, `backups/`, or `.claude/settings.local.json` — so a git-archive-based release approach would auto-exclude those.
partial: Ignore rules are near-complete but miss the malformed local cruft. `backend;C`, `frontend/package.json;C`, and `frontend/package-lock.json;C` all exist locally and are NOT matched by any `.gitignore` pattern (`git check-ignore` reports NOT-ignored for `backend;C` and `frontend/package.json;C`). They stay out of `git archive` only because they're untracked, but a naive `zip -r` release would sweep them in.

OAuth-rotation documentation is thin/scattered, not a runbook. There is a one-line checklist item in `LAUNCH_QA_CHECKLIST.md:31` ('Any credential that ever sat in a shared `.env`/ZIP has been rotated') and a flag in `docs/release-hardening/00-baseline.md:64-66` ('Google OAuth client secret ... Rotate if the `.env` was ever shared/committed/zipped'). `docs/google-login.md` documents OAuth *setup* but contains no rotation steps. No step-by-step procedure exists for rotating the Google OAuth client secret in Google Cloud Console, updating `.env`, and restarting.

`.claude/launch.json` is TRACKED in git (only `.claude/settings.local.json` is gitignored, per `.gitignore:40`). It is local-tooling cruft that ships in any `git archive`. It contains no secret (only an npm dev-server launch config), so it is a cleanliness issue, not a secret leak.
missing: Deterministic release/packaging script: NONE exists. Glob/`git ls-files` for `*.sh`/`*.ps1`/`package`/`release`/`archive` finds only `ops/backup-db.sh` and `ops/restore-db.sh` (DB dump/restore, unrelated to packaging). No git-archive-based release script.

Secret-pattern scanning + fail-on-suspicious-file gate: NONE. No script scans the tree/archive for secret patterns (API keys, client secrets, private-key headers) or aborts when a `.env`/keystore/`*.key` is present. No guarantee-of-not-printing-secrets logic because no such script exists.
Clean-ZIP production excluding all prohibited paths: NONE. No automation produces a release ZIP; the only ZIP handling is `*.zip` in `.gitignore`.

Archive-hygiene verification script: NONE. Nothing unpacks/inspects a produced archive to assert it excludes `.env`, `backups/`, `node_modules`, `target`, `dist`, `.claude/`, `*;C` cruft, and contains no secret patterns.
Formal OAuth (Google client-secret) rotation runbook: MISSING as a standalone documented procedure (see partial note — only one-liners exist).
risks: A hand-rolled `zip -r` release (instead of `git archive`) would leak the untracked local `.env` — it holds 2 populated live secrets (Google OAuth client id + client secret, confirmed via count without printing) — plus `backups/` and the `*;C` cruft. The safe-by-default choice (git archive, tracked-only) is not yet codified in any script, so the outcome depends on whoever runs the release doing it correctly.

`.claude/launch.json` being tracked means it ships in every `git archive` release; harmless today (no secret) but it normalizes shipping local-tooling files and could later carry machine-specific data.
No secret-scanning gate means a future accidental `git add` of a real secret (e.g. someone renaming `.env` to a non-ignored name, or committing a `*;C` variant) would not be caught at package time.

OAuth secret rotation depends on tribal knowledge / one-line reminders; without a runbook the client secret sitting in the local `.env` may never be rotated even though the baseline flags it for manual rotation.
result.recommendation: "1) Build the missing deterministic release script (e.g. `ops/make-release.sh` / `.ps1`) using `git archive --format=zip HEAD -o petpattern-<gitsha>.zip` so only tracked files ship (auto-excludes `.env`, `backups/`, `node_modules`, `target`, `dist`, `*;C` cruft). 2) Before archiving, add a fail-closed pre-flight: abort with non-zero exit if any working-tree/staged path matches `.env`(non-example)/`*.keystore`/`*.jks`/`*.p12`/`*.pem`/`*.key`/`google-services.json`, and run a secret-pattern scan (e.g. `AIza[0-9A-Za-z_-]{35}`, `-----BEGIN * PRIVATE KEY-----`, `GOCSPX-`, generic `client_secret`/high-entropy) over the tracked set — printing only offending FILE PATHS, never values. 3) Add an archive-hygiene verifier that unzips to a temp dir and asserts absence of `.env`, `backups/`, `node_modules`, `target`, `dist`, `.claude/`, `*;C`, plus a secret-pattern re-scan of the archive contents. 4) Stop tracking `.claude/launch.json` (either `git rm --cached` it and broaden `.gitignore` to `.claude/` with a `!.claude/launch.json` only if intentionally shared, or exclude via `.gitattributes export-ignore`), and add `.gitignore` entries for the `*;C` cruft as belt-and-suspenders. 5) Write a short OAuth-rotation runbook (rotate Google client secret in Cloud Console → update `.env` → `docker compose -f docker-compose.prod.yml up -d`), and rotate the secret currently in the local `.env` since it has been present in a shared working tree. 6) Optional: parameterize the `application.yml` local-dev DB password (`password: petpattern`, line 14) with `${SPRING_DATASOURCE_PASSWORD:petpattern}` to avoid any literal credential in tracked source, though prod already overrides it."

implemented: Native image lazy-loading (`loading="lazy"`) is used on tags in PhotosView.jsx:100, TimelineView.jsx:106, PetAvatar.jsx:19, PetPhotoStack.jsx:41 — this is HTML image lazy-loading only, NOT JS code-splitting.

A production build artifact exists to confirm the baseline: frontend/dist/assets/index-DtefeGiF.js is a single 773,638-byte (~756kB) JS chunk plus one 57kB CSS file — matching the stated ~752kB single-chunk baseline.
partial: 'No duplicate dependency chunks' is trivially true only because there is exactly ONE chunk today; it is not a result of any splitting discipline. Once splitting is introduced this requirement becomes real and is currently unaddressed (no manualChunks / vendor strategy in vite.config.js).
missing: Resolve npm audit via safe supported Vite/esbuild update: NOT done. package.json pins `"vite": "^5.4.21"` and the lockfile resolves vite 5.4.21, which bundles esbuild 0.21.5 (vulnerable to GHSA-67mh-4wv8-2f99, dev-server, moderate). No upgrade has been applied.

Route/feature-level lazy loading (patterns, food, photos, vet, caregivers, settings) while keeping Today fast: NOT done. All 20+ feature views are statically imported at the top of App.jsx (lines 30-49) and rendered in a single `view === '...'` conditional block (lines 1048-1206). Everything ships in one chunk.
React.lazy / Suspense: NOT used anywhere in product source. A full grep of frontend/src for `lazy|Suspense|import(` returns only native and one dynamic import in analytics.test.js (test-only).
Loading fallbacks (Suspense boundaries) for lazily-loaded views: NOT present (no Suspense at all).
Chunk-load error handling (retry / reload on a stale-chunk 404 after redeploy): NOT present. No error boundary wraps the view area; App.jsx has per-request try/catch for API calls only.
Measurable initial-bundle reduction: NOT achieved — still a single ~756kB JS chunk. No build-time code-splitting configured (no build.rollupOptions / manualChunks in vite.config.js).
risks: PRE-EXISTING PEER MISMATCH: the lockfile shows vitest 4.1.10 peer-requires vite `^6.0.0 || ^7.0.0 || ^8.0.0` (package-lock.json lines 4553 & 4577), but the project installs vite 5.4.21. The current dependency tree already violates vitest's peer requirement — the Vite-6 upgrade below actually FIXES this rather than introducing new risk.

@vitejs/plugin-react 4.3.4 peer-supports vite `^4.2.0 || ^5.0.0 || ^6.0.0` (package-lock.json line 2276) — it does NOT declare Vite 7. Jumping straight to Vite 7 would also force a plugin-react bump (>=4.4 or 5.x), widening blast radius; Vite 6 is the low-risk target.

Per user memory, there is no local Maven/Java and a plain `docker compose up` serves a STALE frontend — any Vite upgrade + code-split must be validated with an explicit `npm run build` (--build for docker) and the vitest suite, not a plain restart, or regressions will be masked.
The esbuild advisory is dev-server-only (moderate) and does not affect the production bundle, so it is not a shipping-blocker — but it will keep showing in `npm audit` until the Vite bump lands.

@sentry/react 8.55.2 is a large SDK imported eagerly in the entry (main.jsx) even though it is only initialized when VITE_SENTRY_DSN is set — it inflates the initial chunk for every user including dev/no-DSN.

TodayDecisionActions.jsx:16-38, PatternCard.jsx, CheckInView.jsx, CaregiversView.jsx, AccountView.jsx all use native buttons.

Global visible keyboard focus: a single unscoped rule `:focus-visible { outline: 3px solid var(--teal); outline-offset: 2px }` in frontend/src/styles/edit-delete.css:71-74 applies to all interactive elements. base.css:250 sets `outline:none` on inputs but the pseudo-class rule has higher specificity so keyboard focus rings still show. Reinforced for tabs (shell.css:267) and today disclosure (today.css:448).

Destructive-action confirmation on ALL destructive paths via native window.confirm: delete pet (AccountView.jsx:14), delete account with DOUBLE confirm (AccountView.jsx:53-54), remove caregiver (CaregiversView.jsx:61), leave pet (CaregiversView.jsx:15), revoke vet share (VetShareCard.jsx:43), delete check-in (App.jsx:421), delete photo (App.jsx:494), delete trial/medication/food/activity (App.jsx:539,571,582,605).
aria-pressed on every toggle/choice control: QuickChoices.jsx:11, ToggleButton.jsx:5, guided chips CheckInView.jsx:138, VisibleChangeField.jsx:45,61, photo-area buttons PhotosView.jsx:64.
role=group with aria-label on choice grids: QuickChoices.jsx:5, weight unit toggle PetOnboarding.jsx:122, visible-change grid.

Toast is a correct polite live region: components/Toast.jsx:20 `role="status" aria-live="polite"`, plus pause-on-hover/focus so the 3.2s auto-dismiss can't yank focus from a keyboard user, and a labelled dismiss button (aria-label).

Error surfaces are announced: every form/save error uses `<div className="error-box" role="alert">` (App.jsx:976,1046; AuthScreen.jsx:140; CaregiversView.jsx:97,119; AccountView.jsx:77; ResetPasswordView.jsx:75; PetOnboarding.jsx:141).

Reduced-motion honored for all three keyframe animations that exist: styles/today.css:108 (.today-note note-settle), styles/patterns.css:145 (.toast), styles/pet-avatars.css:132 (.pet-photo-stack snap). No uncovered entrance/looping animation was found.

SR-interpretable progress: PatternMemoryProgress.jsx:53 marks the decorative baseline dots `aria-hidden="true"` and pairs them with a text equivalent `{done} of {total} days logged` (line 59), so screen readers get the real progress.
Escape-to-close on all three dismissable overlays: LangToggle.jsx:13, PetSwitcher.jsx:18, PhotosView.jsx:19 (lightbox).

Image alt discipline: decorative avatars use alt="" (PetAvatar.jsx:19, PetPhotoStack.jsx:41, PetIdentityCard.jsx:32); content photos use caption/area-label as alt (PhotosView.jsx:100,120; TimelineView.jsx:106).

Loading/disabled states: submit and action buttons disable while saving/busy/uploading with changed labels — CheckInView.jsx:186,220,224,439; TodayDecisionActions.jsx:16 (disabled when loggedToday); CaregiversView.jsx:99,115; AccountView.jsx:83,96,119; PhotosView.jsx:81.
Accessible collapsibles use native <details>/<summary> (keyboard-operable for free): TodayView.jsx:95 (More about today) and CheckInView.jsx:351 (Optional details).
Reminder permission flow requests Notification permission on enable and reflects granted/denied/blocked/unsupported in visible text: ReminderControl.jsx:35-48 and status copy at 63-77.
Nav landmark and heading structure: `<nav aria-label="PetPattern sections">` App.jsx:1018; consistent h1 per view + h2 section headings.

Most form inputs have real labels via implicit wrapping <label>: onboarding (PetOnboarding.jsx:101,107,116), photos date/caption (PhotosView.jsx:71,75), medications, food, check-in note (CheckInView.jsx:175,455), reminder time (ReminderControl.jsx:58), visible-change note (VisibleChangeField.jsx:68).
partial: Accessible labels are PARTIAL: several key inputs are placeholder-only with no <label>/aria-label, so their accessible name vanishes once typing starts. AuthScreen.jsx:122 (name), :124 (email), :126 (password), and the ResetPassword field; CaregiversView.jsx:109-114 (invite email placeholder only). Login/signup and 'invite a caregiver' are primary flows.

Status/success announcements are PARTIAL: only the Toast is a live region. Non-toast confirmations are plain text with no aria-live, so screen readers don't hear them — AccountView.jsx:78 `{message &&

{message}

}` ('X was deleted', 'Your data has been downloaded'), AuthScreen.jsx:139 reset-link notice, VetShareCard.jsx:79 'Copied' (button text swap). CaregiversView gives NO confirmation at all after an invite is sent (the field just clears).

Touch-target sizing is PARTIAL: primary/secondary/ghost buttons meet ~42-46px (base.css:182,191), but .text-button and .chip-button are 32px (base.css:223) and .icon-button is 34x34 (edit-delete.css:25-26), e.g. the photo delete/close icons (PhotosView.jsx:106,118). These clear the WCAG 2.5.8 AA 24px floor but are under the comfortable 44px; capacitor.css:35-42 raises some to only 40px on native.

Modal semantics are PARTIAL: the only modal (PhotosView lightbox, PhotosView.jsx:117) sets role="dialog" aria-modal="true" and handles Escape, but has NO accessible name (no aria-label/aria-labelledby) so it opens as an unnamed dialog.

Urgent-observation messaging is PARTIAL: the historical urgent banner (TimelineView.jsx:61-68, VetSheet.jsx:166) is coral, iconed and headed 'Worth acting on soon', but uses role="note" — a generic region that is not emphasized or announced as urgent by assistive tech; no aria-live/role=alert/role=status. For a safety-relevant surface this under-conveys urgency to SR users.

ARIA listbox pattern is PARTIAL: LangToggle.jsx:30-32 and PetSwitcher.jsx:49-65 use role="listbox"/role="option" on <button> children with only Escape handling — the pattern implies arrow-key roving focus that isn't implemented. Operable via Tab, but ARIA-inconsistent.
missing: Modal focus trap + focus management is MISSING entirely. The PhotosView lightbox (PhotosView.jsx:116-127) does not move focus into the dialog on open, does not trap Tab within it (focus can walk to the still-present page behind the overlay), and does not restore focus to the triggering thumbnail on close. This is the one true focus-trap requirement in the app and it is unmet.

Programmatic form-error association is MISSING: no aria-invalid, aria-describedby, or aria-errormessage anywhere in src (grep returned zero). Errors render in a page-level role=alert box (announced) but are never tied to the offending field — e.g. the invite email (CaregiversView.jsx:109) has no aria-invalid, so a SR user isn't told which field failed.

Immediate acute/urgent feedback after saving a check-in is MISSING: saveCheckIn (App.jsx:789-808) and quickLog (App.jsx:811-868) only reload data and navigate to Today; nothing surfaces an acute observation at the moment of logging. The urgent banner is historical-only (timeline). This matches WP1 still being in progress, but from the UX side there is no immediate urgent-observation message.
Skip-to-content link is MISSING (grep for skip/Skip found only unrelated 'Skip'/backfill text). Keyboard/SR users must tab through the full header + sidebar nav on every view.
risks: The lightbox is the app's only modal and lacks a focus trap + focus restore; a keyboard/SR user can tab 'behind' the open overlay and lose their place — the highest-impact a11y defect found.
Placeholder-only labels on the sign-in/registration and caregiver-invite inputs mean the accessible name disappears on input; SR users mid-typing lose the field's purpose on primary flows.

The urgent/acute observation banner is role="note" (not a live/alert region), so on a safety-relevant surface the urgency is not conveyed to assistive tech — and there is still no immediate acute message at the moment of logging (ties to WP1 being incomplete).

Success confirmations (deletions, data export, invites sent, link copied) are silent to screen readers because only the Toast is a live region; destructive/irreversible outcomes especially should be announced.

Contrast was not machine-verified in this pass; the design uses warm low-saturation tokens (muted grey text, gold/coral chips) that should be checked against WCAG 1.4.3 4.5:1, particularly `.muted` body text and status chips.
result.recommendation: "1) Add a focus trap to the PhotosView lightbox: on open, move focus to the close button and record the trigger; loop Tab/Shift+Tab within the dialog; on close, restore focus to the triggering thumbnail. Give the dialog an aria-label (e.g. the photo caption/area). This is the single most important fix. 2) Give AuthScreen (name/email/password) and CaregiversView invite inputs real accessible names — visible <label> or at minimum aria-label — instead of placeholder-only. 3) Announce success: reuse the existing Toast pattern (or add role=status/aria-live=polite) for AccountView deletion/export messages, CaregiversView invite-sent, and VetShareCard 'Copied'. 4) Upgrade the urgent-observation banner from role=\"note\" to role=\"status\" (or wrap in an aria-live region) and, for the WP1 immediate layer, surface an acute observation right after saveCheckIn rather than only in the historical timeline. 5) Associate field errors with inputs via aria-invalid + aria-describedby (start with the invite email and auth fields). 6) Add a skip-to-content link ahead of the header nav. 7) Lower-priority: bump .text-button/.chip-button/.icon-button toward 44px hit areas and give LangToggle/PetSwitcher proper arrow-key listbox behavior or drop the listbox roles. 8) Run an automated contrast check on .muted text and status chips."
